snippet.textDisplay:
I am LDS. My religion teaches that there is “no compensation for failure in the family”. No matter how I tried to draw the circle with me on the inside with my family my sister would always redraw the circle with me on the outside. Not understanding that I was part of a family defined by NPD I internalized this failure as my fault.
Now that I know the dynamics of my family, I am learning to not gaslight myself.
I have spent years on and off in therapy with no success because therapy’s goal was to fix me. In my family’s dynamic I was not the one broken, fixing me was not end-goal.
Learning one is not broken is not the end-all to the problem. I would like to see more research done in relationship to the victims of narcissism as opposed to research regarding the narcissist him/herself (especially since treatment for the narcissist has poor outcomes).

Thank you so much for this video. I walked away from a just emotionally abusive sibling situation it took years but cost me also my own daughter and my grands and great grands. As they fell for a massive smear campaign. Hook line and sinker…It was necessary for me to make a decision like that as what was done was too hard to bear. It was done to a younger sibling first. Between a very disconnected mother and abusive older sister who never was told to stop…I tell that younger sister that I can’t believe we survived. The whole life experience cut to the quick. It stole my very life of memories.
I bought myself a small silver cancer survivor emblem to put on a simple necklace. The word “Survivor” is engraved on it. I bought one also for my dearest younger sister( who had the sense to go into no contact in her teen years.) (This was nearly 50 years ago.) ( it took me a little too late to figure that out)
But thank you for your love and encouragement to reach out and help others. It means so much to me and many others to know that someone understands what it is like to be buried under such a mountain of grief. May our Creator bless you.

snippet.textDisplay: I have three of them.  The one thing that I have learned is this, as long as you are entangled with them repeatedly tearing you to the ground and throwing dirt on you over and over you will carry pain and resentment which will affect you in so many negative ways, even your health.  When you walk away and get out of that mess, you will finally be able to love them, and forgive them for everything they have put you through.  You will be able to look to them with pity, and pray heartfelt prayers for their healing, and well being.  It may not be easy to walk away, especially when they are all you have left but that is when God steps in and and begins the process of healing.  You've done your part, let the Almighty do His!  Just keep praying for them to open their spiritual eyes, and desire to change.   ❤

snippet.textDisplay:
So I had lined up a friend to take me to the hospital for knee surgery last Friday. My sister insisted she would do it. I let her take me, but she started in on me the minute she walked in the door.
My sister has become a total conspiracy theorist and knows more than any doctor, nurse, lawyer, historian, ect ect. You cant tell her NOTHING!
Surgery went well she brought me home and I am on crutches attempting to gather my things and belongings and use the crutches and get into bed. She is on the phone watching videos while I am struggling. Petty, but it made me realize that I was the much better choice as a full time live in caregiver for my mom for nearly a year while mom was on hospice.
That weekend my sister went nuts over some shampoo she had left in the upststairs shower being gone. When I say nuts I mean over the top screaming and complaining about this shampoo and then the rant went on to other issues.
My brother and I had overridden her on creating a family trust to put moms estate into. She had stopped this entire process two years prior after we ALL had sat down and met at a round table discussion with the lawyer to set it up. A week later she said NO. Mom was on the hook for the expenses. Fast forward to late 2024 we contacted the lawyer and told him we needed to go through with the trust and she tried to stop it again, but moms health had been steadily failing, so my brother and I vetoed her this time because she wanted to do her OWN private trust with no lawyer. If we waited on her everything would have gone to probate.
Eventually mom had to go into a nursing home as her care became too much for me. I lost all my income and had very little help from either sibling while taking care of mom. Mom fell, ended up in the hospital and the doctor said she had to ho into a nursing home on hospice instead of home hospice.
I looked for homes, visited two and my sister chose one right behind her house. One of the ones I visited was approved by moms hospice and the day of release from the hospital is when my sister came up with her plan. It was too late.
In the end I found out my sister blames me for my moms early demise because I overrode her care home option.
The truth is my sister feels guilty for living her life on her terms doing everything she wanted to do instead of coming to visit her dying mother. (Sis only lived 45 minutes away)The words came out of her mouth the day we went to see the body "I should have come by this past weekend."
I have no regrets or guilt as I did everything I could for my mom but now I killed her in my sisters eyes.
She wants money for her part of everything and to go her own way. No responsibility nor accountability. I got to see just who she truly is and it is sad. We lost mom five months ago now my sister wants to divorce us and go her own way which is what she always did. I went no contact on the 9th of March 2025.
She did all of this ranting and raging while I am recovering from knee surgery. I shake my head at the lack of empathy and the loss of a sibling, but I cannot help her and have to let her go to maintain my own peace and healing.
